Attributable risk from dlnmLPS model

attributable_risk.Rd

This function calculates the attributable risk (attributable fraction and attributable number) from a fitted dlnmLPS model.

Usage

attributable_risk(
  basis,
  cases,
  model,
  cen,
  x,
  y = NULL,
  by = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  dir = "back",
  tot = TRUE,
  range_x = NULL,
  range_y = NULL,
  samples = FALSE,
  nsamples = 1000,
  exc.threshold = NULL
)

Arguments

basis

An object of class "crossbasis" or "joint.crossbasis" defining the exposure-lag basis used in the model.

cases

A vector of cases or, only if dir = "forw", a matrix of future cases.

model

An object of class "dlnmLPS" returned by the dlnmLPS function.

cen

A value (or a vector of length 2 for "joint.crossbasis") specifying the centering (reference) exposure level used for calculating relative risk predictions.

x

Vector of the first exposure or, only if dir = "back" a matrix of lagged exposures, for which the attributable fraction needs to be calculated.

y

Vector of the second exposure or, only if dir = "back" a matrix of lagged exposures, for which the attributable fraction needs to be calculated. Only for basis of class"joint.crossbasis".

by

Vector of the by variable-levels (same length as cases) at which the DLNM relationship is evaluated. For a continuous by variable, this is a vector of numeric values defining the level at which the effect is evaluated. For a factor by variable, this is a vector of factor levels defining the corresponding stratum.

group

Vector of region indicators to specify an optional grouping structure of the output. For spatially varying DLNMs, this argument automatically corresponds to the ID vector in by (i.e., region-specific attributable risks are calculated). For non-spatially varying DLNMs, a vector can also be specified (same length as cases) to group the output per region.

dir

Either "back" (default) or "forw" for backward and forward perspective on attributable risk respectively.

tot

If True, the total attributable risk over the entire period is calculated.

range_x

The range of the first exposure for which the attributable risk is calculated. If NULL(default), the whole range is used.

range_y

The range of the second exposure for which the attributable risk is calculated. If NULL(default), the whole range is used. Only for basis of class"joint.crossbasis".

samples

Set to TRUE if samples from the posterior distribution should be returned. Samples can only be calculated for tot = TRUE.

nsamples

Number of samples from the posterior distribution to be returned. (only when samples = TRUE).

exc.threshold

Numeric value defining the threshold used for exceedance probability calculations of the attributable fraction. If NULL (default), no exceedance probabilities are calculated.

Value

A list containing the attributable fractions and numbers.

If samples = TRUE, the list is structured in two main elements. Note that this option is only possible with tot = TRUE. The two elements are:

samples element

List with samples from the posterior distribution of the total attributable fraction af and total attributable number an. The group ID (if applicable) and exceedance probabilities (if requested) are also reported. For non-NULL grouping structures, this output is structured per group.

fit element

The fitted total af, an, and the group ID if applicable. For non-NULL grouping structures, this output is structured per group.

If samples = FALSE, the list contains the fitted total af, an, and the group ID if applicable, when tot = TRUE. When tot = FALSE, this list contains the day-specific af, an and cases, as well as the group ID if applicable. For non-NULL grouping structures, this output is structured per group.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
data(barcelona_temp)
data(shapefile_bcn)

# Examples of applications

dataset <- barcelona_temp |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    dow = weekdays(date),
    year = lubridate::year(date),
    month = lubridate::month(date)
  )

group <- factor(paste0(dataset$District, "-", dataset$year))


### Example 1: Penalized and common DLNM

# Create the (penalized) crossbasis
basis.max <- dlnm::crossbasis(
    dataset$Tmax,
    argvar = list(df = 5, fun = "ps"),
    arglag = list(df = 5, fun = "ps"),
    lag = 14,
    group = group
)

# Fit model
model_max_common <- dlnmLPS(
    dtot ~ 1 + factor(dow) +
    sm(month, arg = list(type = "ns", df = 3)) +
    sm(year, arg = list(type = "rw1")) +
    sm(basis.max, arg = list(pen= 2)) +
    sm(District, arg = list(type = "Leroux", map = shapefile_bcn)),
    data = dataset,
    offset = log(pop),
    model.comparison = list(DIC = TRUE),
    family = "Poisson"
)

# Calculate attributable fraction (forward perspective) for 2007

data2007_district <- dataset |>
  dplyr::filter(year == 2007)

# Calculate attributable risk
af2007_common <- attributable_risk(
  basis = basis.max,
  cases = data2007_district$dtot,
  model = model_max_common,
  cen = 25,
  x = data2007_district$Tmax,
  group = data2007_district$District, # Calculate af per district
  dir = "forw",
  tot = TRUE,
  samples = TRUE  # Samples from posterior distribution
)

### Example 2: Penalized and common joint DLNM

# Create the (penalized) joint crossbasis
basis.max_min <- joint.crossbasis(
    cbind(dataset$Tmax, dataset$Tmin),
    argvar1 = list(df = 5, fun = "ps"),
    argvar2 = list(df = 5, fun = "ps"),
    arglag = list(df = 5, fun = "ps"),
    lag = 14,
    group = group
)

# Fit model
model_joint_common <- dlnmLPS(
    dtot ~ 1 + factor(dow) +
    sm(month, arg = list(type = "ns", df = 3)) +
    sm(year, arg = list(type = "rw1")) +
    sm(basis.max_min, arg = list(pen= 2)) +
    sm(District, arg = list(type = "Leroux", map = shapefile_bcn)),
    data = dataset,
    offset = log(pop),
    model.comparison = list(DIC = TRUE),
    family = "Poisson"
)

# Calculate attributable fraction (backward perspective) for 2007

af2007_joint <- attributable_risk(
  basis = basis.max_min,
  cases = data2007_district$dtot,
  model = model_joint_common,
  cen = c(25,15),
  x = data2007_district$Tmax,
  y = data2007_district$Tmin,
  group = data2007_district$District, # Calculate af per district
  dir = "back",
  tot = TRUE,
  samples = TRUE  # Samples from posterior distribution
)


### Example 3: Unpenalized and spatially varying DLNM

# Create the (unpenalized) crossbasis
knots_max <- quantile(dataset$Tmax, probs = c(0.10,0.50,0.90))
knots_lag <- dlnm::logknots(0:14, nk = 2)

basis.max_unpen <- dlnm::crossbasis(
    dataset$Tmax,
    argvar=list(fun = "ns", knots = knots_max),
    arglag=list(fun="ns", knots = knots_lag),
    lag=14,
    group=group
)

# Fit model
model_max_spat <- dlnmLPS(
    dtot ~ 1 + factor(dow) +
    sm(month, arg = list(type = "ns", df = 3)) +
    sm(year, arg = list(type = "rw1")) +
    sm(basis.max_unpen, by = District,
            arg.by = list(type = "Leroux", map = shapefile_bcn)) +
    sm(District, arg = list(type = "Leroux", map = shapefile_bcn)),
    data = dataset,
    offset = log(pop),
    model.comparison = list(DIC = TRUE),
    family = "Poisson")


# Calculate attributable fraction (backward perspective) for 2007

af2007_spat <- attributable_risk(
  basis = basis.max_unpen,
  cases = data2007_district$dtot,
  model = model_max_spat,
  cen = 25,
  x = data2007_district$Tmax,
  by = data2007_district$District, # Spatially varying DLNM by district
  dir = "back",
  tot = TRUE,
  samples = TRUE  # Samples from posterior distribution
)


### Example 4: Unpenalized and deprivation-varying DLNM

# Fit model
model_max_conf <- dlnmLPS(
    dtot ~ 1 + factor(dow) +
    sm(month, arg = list(type = "ns", df = 3)) +
    sm(year, arg = list(type = "rw1")) +
    sm(depriv, arg = list(type = "ns", df = 3)) +
    sm(basis.max_unpen, by = depriv,
            arg.by = list(type = "ns", df = 3)) +
    sm(District, arg = list(type = "Leroux", map = shapefile_bcn)),
    data = dataset,
    offset = log(pop),
    model.comparison = list(DIC = TRUE),
    family = "Poisson")

# Calculate attributable fraction (forward perspective) for 2007

af2007_conf <- attributable_risk(
  basis = basis.max_unpen,
  cases = data2007_district$dtot,
  model = model_max_conf,
  cen = 25,
  x = data2007_district$Tmax,
  by = data2007_district$depriv, # By-value for every district
  group = data2007_district$District, # Group output by district
  dir = "forw",
  tot = TRUE,
  samples = TRUE  # Samples from posterior distribution
)
} # }
